direction.analyst: Claude, as the analyst of one game for the market reports handler, 27 Nov 2026: from the run's 57 contact sheets (every one opened), the skeleton files' own data and 29 real screens of the game played by the analyst. This run reads Blueprint Gaming's build BP_TheGooniesQuestForTreasure295 of the same title; the market report ranks White Hat Studios' US build (WHS_TheGooniesQuestForTreasure2US94), whose demo is behind a client login. That the art is the same in both builds is inference. It is not the Jackpot Royale version, which is a separate game.
direction.summary: A licensed film adventure staged as a lantern-lit pirate cave: realistic painted portraits of the film's characters and a skeleton pirate host set among cartoon-bold gold lettering and jewel-bright treasure, almost entirely warm orange and gold against one navy reel board, with cyan and acid green kept as signal colours.
direction.style: Two registers side by side. Likeness art (four portrait symbols and one full-length figure) is semi-realistic film-poster painting. Everything else is stylised painted cartoon realism: props such as chests, coins, a ship's wheel, scrolls and chains painted with full materials, and a faceted, animation-background cave. One-Eyed Willy, a skull in a green tricorn hat with a gold eye patch, is the mascot and appears as symbol, map icon, intro host and transition mark.
direction.rendering: Fully painted, no line outlines on objects; heavy dark outlines only on lettering. Props carry real material detail (wood grain, rust, hammered metal) at small sizes with hard top-left highlights. The cave is flat faceted planes with soft gradients only in light. Light effects are separate soft additive pictures (the files sit on black or are plain glows), so glow is a layer, not paint.
direction.colour: Measured over the game's own art: black-brown #1c0c0c 19%, brown #572817 18% and #8e4b23 15%, then light gold #f8eb87 3% and one dark blue #273145 2%. Almost every unit measures 80 to 100% warm. The reel board is the exception (dark blue #152035, 94% of its unit) and is what the gold symbols are read against. Identity colours are used as codes, not decoration: blue, red and green for the three chests and their bonus symbols; gold, green, red and blue for the four collectors; yellow, green, blue and red for the four jackpot plates; cyan (#0cceff) for anticipation and One-Eyed Willy Spins; acid green (#53ff60, #78ff0b) for the Mystery Symbol and the lock.
direction.lighting: The scene has three lights by colour: orange from the skull-shaped cave mouth and two lanterns, teal-green daylight behind the stair, purple in the shadowed rock, with a warm pool on the floor under the reels. Objects are lit from the top left. Prizes glow from inside (coin heaps, the ruby, the chests), and every win or feature state is an added coloured light in the object's own shape.
direction.ambience: Adventure, not horror: a treasure hunt by lantern light, with skeletons played for fun and the film's catchphrases (NEVER SAY DIE!, HEY YOU GUYS!) used as art. The board always shows the long game: the trail map above and the three chests beside the reels.
direction.shapes: Chunky and irregular: hand-cut slab letters, torn parchment, hammered coins with uneven rims, faceted rock. The reel cell is a wide 215x180 rectangle, 6 reels by 4 rows; the collector grows from one cell to a 215x720 column. Round medallions and rectangles with value plates repeat across the prize symbols.
direction.materials: Parchment and turned wood with brass caps (scrolls, map), dark ship planks (board, panels), gold in three finishes (hammered doubloon, stamped skull coin, plain cartoon disc), ruby and cut gems, rusted iron (chains, the Treasure Wheel), bone, cobweb, lantern glass.
direction.typography: Four lettering families, all as pictures or bitmap fonts (nine font pages with BMFont .xml files; the only embedded web font is the shell's Roboto Black). A curly storybook pirate serif for values and counters; fat comic block capitals with gradient, extrusion and dark outline for feature names, each in its identity colour; angular faceted slab numerals in gold for win amounts and in silver for free-spin counts; and wide serif capitals that look cut from rusted copper for the big-win tiers. The logo is the film's own lettering.
direction.motion: 68 Spine skeletons, 62 of them version 4.1.24 (three 4.1.17 for the max-win notice, one 4.1.23, and two 3.8 for the shared Power Play art), plus 8 frame sequences of 19 to 30 frames (fire-line win boxes, win blast, dynamite, coin spin, coin burst, burning plate). The rigs are small (most under 35 bones; the unlock pop-up has 66) and move whole pictures: symbols land in 0.3 s and play a 1.0 s win, the collector grows in 1.1 s, the chests have 45 short state animations each, the background runs one 233 s loop of light. No character is rigged limb by limb: the one full figure is a still swung on a rope. None of the skeletons is drawn in this run, because the project's renderer does not draw Spine 4.x; the real game screens show the motion's key states.
direction.variants: Variation is by recolour and by swap. One bonus chest in four colours; one collector in four colours and two heights; three chests from one drawing; four jackpot plates from one frame; five big-win tiers that differ only in the word; eight unlock screens from one scroll. Every reel symbol up to the portraits has a blurred twin for the spinning reel. A landscape and a portrait skeleton exist for the intro, chests, pots and pop-ups, over the same pictures.
direction.construction: 726 loose pictures in named folders, no atlas pages at all, at one scale (folder 100). Each feature is a folder with its skeletons and an images folder, and the client loads a feature's folder when it first needs it: 77 pictures and 5 skeletons arrived only during play. Backgrounds are single 3200x3200 squares cropped by the viewport. Text that carries language is baked into pictures marked _ml. Several pictures are shipped twice under different folders (the trail icons, the rope figure, the explosion).
direction.consistency: Strong in colour and material: almost nothing leaves the orange-gold-brown family except by rule. Weaker in drawing hands: the realistic portraits, the cartoon props and a flat vector max-win notice are three styles, and there are three different coin designs. Leftover names from other Blueprint games (banana_trail, kong, genie_hammer_hit) and a ruby coin that reads SUPER for every pot show a shared production kit under the licensed skin (inference).
takeaways: Read this as Blueprint Gaming's build BP_TheGooniesQuestForTreasure295. The market report ranks White Hat Studios' US build (WHS_TheGooniesQuestForTreasure2US94); the two share a title, and that they share their art is inference. It is not the Jackpot Royale version.

The licence carries the faces, the logo and two catchphrases; everything else is ordinary pirate-treasure art that a studio could make for its own theme: a cave, chests, coins, a map, a skeleton host. The lesson is how little likeness art (four portraits and one still figure) is needed to make a licensed game feel like the film.
One cool surface in a warm game: the navy reel board (#152035) is the only large cool area, so gold and orange symbols read without outlines. Worth copying as a layout rule.

Colour as code: three chest colours, four collector colours and four pot colours are each used the same way everywhere they appear (symbol, title, glow, pop-up), and cyan and acid green are reserved for anticipation and for the mystery and lock states.

Persistent progress drawn as objects, not meters: a parchment map of 20 steps above the reels and three physical chests beside them, each step paying off with its own titled unlock screen. For AI art work this is a set of small, flat, high-contrast icons plus one reusable scroll.

Variants by recolour and swap: one drawing per idea (chest, collector, plate, banner), then colour sets and word pictures. An art package planned this way needs few masters and many cheap derivatives, which suits generating a master and deriving variants.

Motion is cheap here: small Spine 4.1 rigs that move whole pictures, additive glow layers and a handful of short frame sequences; no rigged character. A studio can match this level of animation without character rigging.

Production notes for our own packages: lazy loading by feature folder keeps the first load light (649 pictures at start, 77 more in play); square 3200 px backgrounds serve both orientations; baked-in language pictures (_ml) make every language a new set of files.

Not seen in this run, so not to be relied on from it: free spins (Treasure Spins and One-Eyed Willy Spins), the Treasure Wheel, a big win and Power Play in play. Their art is in the package and read from the sheets only.

Reels turning with blurred symbols; a stack of cash coins (15.00, 15.00, 3.50, 2.50), a ruby coin reading SUPER and a blue BONUS chest already landed.
The unlock scroll over the teal-tinted cave: UNLOCKED! CASCADE COLLECT NOW ACTIVE! CASH FALLS AWAIT! beside a tall green Willy tile.
The intro scroll over the teal-tinted cave: the trail icons in a row, One-Eyed Willy at the left, UPGRADE TRAIL, JOURNEY ALONG THE UPGRADE TRAIL UNLOCKING UPGRADES ALONG THE WAY.
